text:
### Observed differences

- The activities occupying the middle of the process changed: in the earlier window A21, A22 and A23 each appeared in about 20 in 100 traces, and in the later window in about 80 in 100; conversely, A24, A25 and A26 each fell from about 80 in 100 traces to about 20–22 in 100. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]

- The old trio's ties dissolved in the later window: pairs among A24/A25/A26 co-occurred in about 82 in 100 traces earlier and in only about 21 in 100 later (about 78 in 100 contain neither), and their co-occurrence with the anchors A20, A30, A34 and A35 dropped the same way, leaving the anchor alone in about 78–79 in 100 traces. [REL038, REL039, REL043, REL014, REL040, REL041, REL044]

- The new trio shows the mirror image: pairs among A21/A22/A23 went from about 19 in 100 co-occurring (about 80 in 100 neither) to about 79 in 100, with both execution orders roughly equally frequent; A20 now precedes each of them in about 77 in 100 shared traces (about 18–19 before), they precede A34 and A35 in about 77–79 in 100 (about 19 before), and they interleave with A30 in about 34 in 100 traces (about 6 before). [REL017, REL018, REL025, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL023, REL030, REL036, REL024, REL031, REL037, REL022, REL029, REL035]

- A20's outgoing transitions shifted accordingly: earlier about 82 in 100 went to A24, A25 or A26; in the later window about 78 in 100 go to A21, A22 or A23. [DIR005]

- The two trios behave as alternatives, not companions: for pairs such as A21–A24, A22–A25 or A23–A26, about 80 in 100 earlier traces contained only the old-trio activity and about 78 in 100 later traces only the new-trio activity, while joint occurrence stays near 0–1 in 100 in both windows. [REL019, REL020, REL026, REL027, REL032, REL033, REL034]

- The A06 branch after A34 closed: earlier about 44 in 100 of A34's outgoing transitions went to A06, which then preceded A35 in about 44 in 100 of its shared traces, and A06 appeared in about 46 in 100 traces overall; later about 90 in 100 of A34's outgoing transitions go straight to A35, A35 follows A34 within one step in about 92 in 100 cases (about 56 before), A06's participation fell to about 12 in 100, and its own exits spread from almost only A35 (about 92 in 100) across several targets. [DIR006, LAG006, REL010, OCC003, DIR001]

- Smaller differences: A02 and A04 roughly doubled in participation but remain rare (about 8→17 and 5→19 in 100 traces); A34's position is essentially unchanged (present in all traces, median about 0.94–0.95) with slightly more spread; A06's few remaining executions sit earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.52 versus 0.91); some profiles (A08's outgoing shares, lags around A06) rest on only 1–26 later-window observations. [OCC001, OCC002, POS003, POS001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the typical case runs A20, then the trio A21/A22/A23 (executed together in varying order and interleaved with A30), then A34 and immediately A35 — whereas in the earlier window the typical case ran A20, then A24/A25/A26, then A34 and, in roughly 44 in 100 cases, A06 before A35. The new trio rose from about 20 to about 80 in 100 traces, the old trio fell from about 82 to about 20–22, A20's successors moved directly from the old trio to the new one, and the A34 → A06 exit all but disappeared in favour of an immediate A34 → A35 step. The signs are direct and mutually consistent — participation counts, co-occurrence and ordering profiles, and the successor changes at A20 and A34 — around anchors (A20, A30, A34, A35) that appear in every trace in both windows; moreover, 73 qualifying items against roughly 1 expected without change, each difference larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, cannot be explained by sampling variation alone. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, DIR005, DIR006, LAG006, REL017, REL036, REL019, OCC003]

The evidence shows which behaviour changed but not how it came about: it cannot distinguish one coordinated restructuring from independent changes that added the new trio and removed the old one, and it cannot exclude that both trios were already alternative paths (the new one ran in about 20 in 100 earlier traces) whose shares flipped; details of A06's residual behaviour rest on only about 12–26 traces in 100. [REL017, OCC003, DIR001]

Other differences: A02 and A04 became somewhat more frequent but stay rare; A34's position shows a slight increase in variability; A08's outgoing profile changed, though on few observations. [OCC001, OCC002, POS003, DIR002]
